title: Room and Hymn
premise: Dominic Blackwood, a pest controller who has spent a decade rationalizing the noises in his late grandmother's house, inherits the property and discovers reel-to-reel sleep recordings from 1974 in which a second voice answers questions no one asked aloud. The voice belongs to something that was fed — given a room, a name, and hymns sung to it nightly — until the family took back what they promised and sealed it behind the wallpaper of the upstairs bedroom. As frost spreads across the house in patterns shaped like fingerprints, Dominic learns he is the last Blackwood, the intended replacement for the child the thing lost, and must return the stolen heirloom locket buried in the cellar before the final frost pattern completes itself. He does return it, at terrible cost: the voice is freed, but it chooses to stay, and Dominic — who never belonged anywhere — finally has a family, even if it hums through the walls.
about_author: N. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former building inspector from rural Vermont who spent years documenting houses that 'behaved wrong.' Their fiction blends procedural detail with folk horror, and they claim every story begins with a real floor plan.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Called to inspect scratching in an elderly client's walls, Dominic finds claw-shaped wear marks at exactly hand height and tells himself it's raccoons. The client mentions the previous exterminator quit mid-job in 1974. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking at its first seam.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. His grandmother dies and leaves him her house — the same house from the callout, he realizes with dread. Moving in, he hears the familiar nocturnal sounds he's spent ten years explaining away, now louder, patient. Emotional beat: grief tangled with the suspicion that he was always meant to come back.

chapters.title: Reels
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the attic he finds labeled reels: 'SLEEP — NIGHTLY.' Playing one, he hears his grandmother's breathing, then a second voice answering questions she never spoke aloud. It asks about 'the boy.' Emotional beat: ten years of rationalizations collapsing in eleven minutes of tape.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, with flashback passages in his grandmother's voice via journal entries. He learns of a 1974 bargain: the family promised their stillborn son's memory-keeper — a locket — to the thing in exchange for protection, then reneged and sealed the nursery. Emotional beat: horror curdling into inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Winter arrives early; frost blooms on the inside of windows in shapes like whorled fingerprints, each night more complete. The upstairs door, painted shut for decades, stands open. Emotional beat: the house shifting from container to countdown.

chapters.title: Hymn for a Small Room
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Dominic and the voice (rendered in second person). The voice recounts being sung to, named, loved — then abandoned. It doesn't want to hurt him; it wants to be answered. Emotional beat: terror giving way to an unbearable tenderness.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Remember
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A found-family thread: the elderly neighbor Marge, the retired priest Father Okafor, and the hardware store owner reveal the town always knew and looked away. They offer to help — the first people who've ever chosen him. Emotional beat: belonging arriving sideways, in crisis.

chapters.title: The Cellar Shelf
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Digging beneath the cellar floor, he unearths the locket — and the small bones beside it, which are not his uncle's. The frost pattern completes except for one print. The voice stops humming; the silence is worse. Emotional beat: the cost of the truth made physical.

chapters.title: Return
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, climax. On the longest night, he carries the locket into the sealed nursery as the frost writes its final finger across the glass. He offers it back, offers himself as the replacement, and sings the hymn off-key and alone. The voice must choose: take him or forgive. Emotional beat: surrender as courage.

chapters.title: Room and Hymn
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, resolution. The voice takes the locket and releases him — but stays, choosing the house over freedom. Spring comes; the frost prints melt. Dominic keeps the house, keeps the recordings, keeps the nightly hymn, and lets Marge and Okafor in. Emotional beat: a found family, human and otherwise, humming through the walls.
